title: Proposal: Implement end-to-end password hashing element in HTML

labels.name: security/privacy
labels.description: There are security or privacy implications

body:
Hello folk:

Currently, there is a fundamental security problem with HTML. All element `<input type=password>` has access to the password in plain text via the DOM or when the input is send to the backend in a form. It gives a false sense of privacy and security to the user. The users think the password will not be shown to anyone because of the stars, and does not guarantee the website owner will hash the password and not look at it.

There is a torrent file that's being distributed over the internet with around 100 billion records. The torrent contains usernames/emails and passwords. I think some lot of developers don't hash and salt the passwords correctly. When badly written website get hacked, the result is catastrophic. Lot of users might gave used the same password for emails, bank..etc.

I suggest implement a new type for password input with end-to-end password hashing. When the user enter their password, the browser hashes the password and make it available in a hashed string format like this: "ab:63:aa..." 

The new type should have the following:

1-hash_function: This type accept the current NIST standard hash functions or debug mode. If the hash function in debug mode, the password can be viewed in a plaintext. However, a warning pops to the user the password input is insecure. 
 
2-salt: The salt that will be used with the password. The minimum salt requirement should be high enough to prevent rainbow[1] attack.

The following are used to enforce password complexity requirements. The browser stores metadata about the password element that can be used verify password requirements.

2-password_length: The length of the password.

3-has_number: 
Check if the password has a number.

4-has_lower_letter: 
Check if the password has lower case letter.

5-has_upper_letter:
Check if the password has upper case letter.

6-has_symbols:
Check if the password has symbols.

`<password hash_function="sha256" minimum_length=10>`

Let me know what do you think. 

Reference
1-https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_table
